clue.text: Cut down service area

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a measure of area

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a motorway service station has been reduced in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service area' reads as a motorway stop, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre people is to slaughter them, and to cut down is to kill in numbers.

clue.text: Slough man treating big guns with some craft

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a man who treats patients
RA is the Royal Artillery, the big guns
SS is a steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A man in Slough deals with heavy artillery with some skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough reads as the English town but means a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, a quagmire.

clue.text: Sardonic humour when turning weary

indicators.note: turning means the word for when is read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: Dry wit appears when someone gets tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mockery using irony and ridicule.

clue.text: The defence simply wasn't there

parts.note: describes a plea that the accused was elsewhere at the time of the crime

explanation.surface: A football team's backline failed to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' suggests sport, but it is a legal plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere when a crime happened.

clue.text: One read out for school assembly

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pupil reads aloud at morning assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' looks like reciting; ONE READ is rearranged. 'Assembly' points to putting letters together. Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known independent girls' boarding school near Brighton.

clue.text: Bring in MP-or it might appear so

indicators.note: says the printed letters could turn into the answer if shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the letters M, P, O and R as printed, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A playful suggestion that an MP might be brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MP-OR IT rearrange into the answer; the odd hyphen hints the printed letters are the material.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them into a country from abroad.

clue.text: Mister Knockabout!

explanation.surface: A pantomime clown's stage name.
explanation.walkthrough: Mister is a title, or handle, for a man; knockabout means rough treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is a form of address for a man, his title; knockabout handling is rough physical treatment.

clue.text: Against just sitting after work

indicators.note: after means the sitting word comes after the work word

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posing is sitting for an artist without doing anything else

explanation.surface: Someone objects to lazing about after their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just sitting' means modelling for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing means set against something, contrary to it.

clue.text: Fliers making childish complaint over quarters

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: thrush is a fungal infection common in babies
E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Pilots grumble like children about their living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests lodgings, but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrushes are songbirds, which fly.

clue.text: Annoyed about a Greek character being told

indicators.note: about means the word for annoyed goes round the Greek letter

parts.note: riled means annoyed
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a story about a person from Greece being related to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to recount it, so retailed means narrated.

clue.text: A person shooting birds, having the right

parts.note: snipe are wading birds, and the plural is unchanged
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A hunter who shoots game birds and has the right to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a licensed game shoot, but the birds give letters rather than a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who fires from a hidden position.

clue.text: The woman in overall command

indicators.note: in says the name is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman is in charge of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's first name, so it can stand for an unnamed woman.

clue.text: Divination of the kind that is without support

parts.note: sort means kind or type

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters for that is wrap round the support

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A form of fortune-telling with nothing to back it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so 'that is' wraps round the support.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is foretelling the future by drawing lots, a method of prophecy.

clue.text: A rider is all for a recess

parts.note: taken as written
a rider is an addition to a document, like a PS or postscript
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone riding a horse is keen on a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman, but it is an addendum, here PS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is a semicircular niche or apse in a church wall.

clue.text: One will get into a vehicle if idle

indicators.note: says the letter for one is placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a van if they have nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or fruitless, as with idle threats, matching a vain attempt.

clue.text: A Pole sent off to get certain animals

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Polish man is dispatched to fetch some beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A POLE SENT is rearranged; 'sent off' suggests a football dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are horned grazing mammals of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Rather slow, neat, and affected

indicators.note: affected suggests something artificially altered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A description of a dancer who is a bit sluggish, tidy and pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NEAT and AND gives the answer; 'affected' looks like a third adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderately slow walking pace.

clue.text: Fool the heartless in the end as agreed

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the word for end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless means removing the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A silly person without feeling finally agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips the middle letter from 'the', and 'in' puts what is left inside 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assented means gave consent, said yes.

clue.text: Personal representation

parts.note: a depiction of an individual person, as in a painting

explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a particular person.

clue.text: Ronald's retired and Edward's expressed some dissatisfaction

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, so the letters for Ronald's are reversed

parts.note: Ron is short for Ronald, and the possessive adds an S
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Ronald has gone to bed and Edward has grumbled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work or going to bed, but it turns RONS back to SNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorting is making a loud scornful sound through the nose, a show of contempt.

clue.text: Follow direction given by a Venetian luminary

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone follows the advice of a famous Venetian.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice, its leading figure.

clue.text: Cook a little lunch effortlessly

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a small midday meal with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a kitchen.

clue.text: Noisy but quite possibly calm worker

indicators.note: suggests the word calm could become something else when its letters are mixed

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a colony

explanation.surface: A labourer may be loud yet relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means clamorous, loud and insistent.

clue.text: Get into trouble over a glass of sherry

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: cop it is British slang for be punished or get into trouble

explanation.surface: Someone is reprimanded over a sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop it' is British slang for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is a tulip-shaped glass used for sherry.

clue.text: Uncompromising view taken about a minister's rise

indicators.note: says the word for view surrounds the reversed title

parts.note: to see is to view

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is a title for a minister

explanation.surface: A stern opinion is formed about a clergyman's promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' suggests a clergyman's promotion, but in a down clue it turns the title upwards; 'taken about' puts the view word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh and strict, refusing to soften.

clue.text: Praise accorded formerly to the Left

parts.note: ex means formerly, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Approval was once given to the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' reads as politics, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to speak highly of someone, to laud them.

clue.text: Ostentatious old monarch does-in a fashion

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A showy former king kills someone in his own style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does in' looks like a murder, but the hyphenated word plus 'a' is fodder for 'fashion'. GR (Georgius Rex) is a crossword convention for an old king.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose describes something showy and pretentiously imposing.

clue.text: Cover many a crop

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, many
rape is an oilseed crop

explanation.surface: Many farmers protect a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape is to hang cloth over something, to cover it.

clue.text: Disreputable individuals storm in the back way

indicators.note: in means the word for storm sits inside the turned letters
back means the abbreviation for way is read backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ramp is to rage or storm about

explanation.surface: Shady characters burst in through the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The back way' sounds like a rear door; 'back' turns the street abbreviation round, and 'in' sets the storm word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are vagrants or vagabonds, people of no fixed home or good name.

clue.text: Father tries a different arrangement for a dependant

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: says the following letters are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A father attempts to reorganise things for someone who relies on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different arrangement' is the anagram signal on 'tries a'; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another, a hanger-on who relies on a host.

clue.text: Shudder at reading of French trial

parts.note: de is French for of
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone recoils on reading about a court case in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French trial' looks like one unit, but 'of French' gives DE and 'trial' gives TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe it, to recoil from it in disgust.

clue.text: Accommodation for indigent travellers in the main

definitions.text: Accommodation for indigent travellers in the main

parts.words: Accommodation for indigent travellers in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this describes the cheapest quarters on a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Where poor passengers mostly stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class on an ocean liner, used by poor emigrants.
